documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea and Edema
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, short of breath, legs swelling.

HPI: Over roughly the last two months he has been more tired, gets winded walking up his driveway or carrying groceries, and both lower legs have been swelling, worse by evening. Home scale up about 6-7 lb over that time. No chest pain or pressure, no palpitations, no fainting. No fever or cough. Taking all medicines, no new ones, no extra salt that he can think of. Back pain stable.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40 qAM, ASA 81, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as recorded, weight up from December. No distress at rest. JVP hard to judge with his neck habitus. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Pitting edema both legs to the mid-shin.

A/P:
1. Progressive exertional dyspnea, fatigue and bilateral edema in a man with HFrEF and CAD - needs cardiology evaluation and a new echo. Spoke with the cardiology office; seen on 1/18. They will draw labs and do the echo there.
2. BP above his usual today; recheck at cardiology.
3. Daily weights, low-salt diet reviewed. Go to the ED for chest pain, breathlessness at rest, or inability to lie flat.

reports.text:
TRANSTHORACIC ECHOCARDIOGRAM
Indication: heart failure with worsening dyspnea and edema.
Left ventricle: ventricular walls are increased in thickness. Chamber size is normal. LVEF 38%.
Diastolic function: impaired left ventricular filling.
Right ventricle: normal size.
Valves: no significant valvular abnormality; no significant stenosis or regurgitation.
Atria: not dilated.
Pericardium: no effusion.
reports.conclusion: Thickened ventricular walls, normal-sized chambers, impaired diastolic filling, LVEF 38%. No significant valve disease.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 01/18/2021
Referring: primary care

Dear colleague,

Thank you for asking me to see Mr. Clark, a 68-year-old man with coronary disease (LAD stent 2015), heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3b, a 2017 stroke and recently diagnosed lumbar stenosis, seen for two months of rising fatigue, breathlessness with exertion and swelling of both legs. He has had no chest pain, palpitations or syncope.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: father MI at 62 and hypertension; mother type 2 diabetes and stroke at 70; no amyloidosis or autoimmune disease.
Social: never smoker; no alcohol now; retired accountant.

Exam: BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 18. Jugular venous pressure elevated. On auscultation there is a low-pitched rumble in diastole at the apex. Lungs clear. Pitting edema 2+ to the mid-shins on both sides.

Labs today: creatinine 2.1 mg/dL and BUN 45 mg/dL; albumin low at 3.2 g/dL while total protein is high at 8.5 g/dL. Urinalysis positive for protein without blood or casts.

Echocardiogram today: thickened ventricular walls, normal-sized chambers, impaired diastolic filling, LVEF 38%, no significant valve disease.

Impression: Heart failure with congestion. The combination of thick walls with a normal-sized cavity and restrictive filling, proteinuria, low albumin and a high total protein raises concern for an infiltrative process, specifically amyloidosis, rather than ischemic progression alone.

Plan:
1. Serum protein electrophoresis with immunofixation and serum free light chains sent today.
2. Referral to hematology, to be expedited if the studies show a monoclonal protein.
3. No medication changes today; daily weights; low sodium diet.
4. I will see him back after hematology.

Cardiology

documents.title: Outside Lab Results - Protein Studies
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Results received by fax from the cardiology office (collected 01/18/2021):
- Serum protein electrophoresis: M-protein 1.8 g/dL
- Immunofixation: IgG lambda monoclonal protein
- Free lambda light chain 186 mg/L, free kappa 11 mg/L, kappa/lambda ratio 0.06
Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Results Discussion
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Mr. Clark about the protein studies cardiology sent. There is an abnormal IgG lambda protein and a very high lambda light chain. Together with the echo and urine protein, cardiology and I are concerned about AL amyloidosis. Explained this is a blood-cell (plasma cell) problem that can deposit protein in the heart and kidneys, that it is treatable, and that hematology needs to confirm it with a biopsy. Cardiology already arranged hematology for 2/11. He asked good questions, wrote everything down. Will call him after the hematology visit.

documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of service: 02/11/2021
Referred by: cardiology; copy to primary care

Reason: IgG lambda monoclonal protein with cardiac and renal findings concerning for AL amyloidosis.

History: 68-year-old man with HFrEF, CAD with LAD stent, CKD 3b, hypertension, type 2 diabetes and prior stroke. Two to three months of progressive fatigue, exertional dyspnea and leg edema. Cardiology echo 01/18 showed thickened walls with a normal-sized cavity, impaired filling and LVEF 38%. Urine protein positive; albumin 3.2, total protein 8.5. SPEP M-protein 1.8 g/dL, IgG lambda; free lambda 186 mg/L, kappa 11 mg/L, ratio 0.06.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, furosemide 40 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, aspirin 81 mg, acetaminophen PRN.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: no amyloidosis or autoimmune disease.

Today: NT-proBNP 4850 pg/mL, high-sensitivity troponin T 62 ng/L. 24-hour urine collection started; result 2.4 g protein per 24 hours.

Exam: edema 2+ both legs. No macroglossia. No periorbital bruising.

Assessment: Lambda light chain monoclonal gammopathy with a phenotype strongly suggesting systemic AL amyloidosis involving the heart and kidneys.

Plan:
1. Abdominal fat pad aspirate with Congo red and amyloid typing.
2. Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy.
3. Return after both results to discuss treatment.

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: abdominal subcutaneous fat pad, fine-needle aspirate.
Gross: multiple fragments of yellow adipose tissue.
Microscopic: adipose tissue with amorphous extracellular deposits around small vessels and between fat cells. Congo red stain positive with apple-green birefringence under polarized light.
Amyloid typing (laser microdissection with mass spectrometry, reference laboratory): AL (lambda) type.
reports.conclusion: Abdominal fat pad: amyloid deposits, Congo red positive; typed as AL lambda.

documents.title: Pathology Received - Fat Pad Aspirate
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fat pad aspirate pathology report received from hematology (procedure 02/25/2021). Scanned to Media and routed to PCP.

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy, posterior iliac crest.
Microscopic: normocellular marrow with trilineage hematopoiesis. Plasma cells are increased, about 12% of cellularity, and are lambda light chain restricted by in situ hybridization. Congo red stain shows positive deposits in vessel walls.
Flow cytometry: monotypic lambda plasma cell population.
reports.conclusion: Bone marrow with 12% lambda-restricted plasma cells and Congo red positive vascular deposits, consistent with AL amyloidosis.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up - Diagnosis and Plan
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 03/11/2021

Results reviewed with Mr. Clark:
- Fat pad aspirate (02/25): Congo red positive, apple-green birefringence; mass spectrometry typing AL lambda.
- Bone marrow (03/04): 12% lambda-restricted plasma cells; Congo red positive vascular deposits.
- Free lambda 186 mg/L, kappa 11 mg/L, ratio 0.06; M-protein 1.8 g/dL IgG lambda.
- NT-proBNP 4850 pg/mL, hs-troponin T 62 ng/L; 24-hour urine protein 2.4 g.
- Echo: thickened walls, normal cavity, impaired filling, LVEF 38%.

Diagnosis: Systemic AL (lambda) amyloidosis with cardiac and renal involvement.

Discussion: Given the degree of cardiac involvement and his kidney function he is not a candidate for high-dose chemotherapy with stem cell rescue. We discussed daratumumab with cyclophosphamide, bortezomib and dexamethasone as standard first-line therapy, its goals (stopping new light chain production so organ function can stabilize), side effects (infusion reactions, neuropathy, infection, glucose rise with dexamethasone) and the schedule. He wishes to proceed.

Plan:
1. Dara-CyBorD starting 03/15/2021, 28-day cycles x 6:
   - daratumumab 1800 mg subcutaneous weekly cycles 1-2, every 2 weeks cycles 3-6, then every 4 weeks to complete two years
   - bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 subcutaneous weekly
   - cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m2 IV weekly
   - dexamethasone 20 mg by mouth weekly (reduced dose for cardiac involvement)
2. Acyclovir 400 mg twice daily for zoster prophylaxis.
3. Free light chains each cycle. Weekly CBC on treatment.
4. Dexamethasone will raise his sugars - primary care aware; continue home glucose checks.
5. Cardiology co-managing volume.

Medications otherwise unchanged: lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, furosemide 40 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: none known.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here to go over the new diagnosis and how we coordinate. Hematology confirmed systemic AL amyloidosis (lambda) with heart and kidney involvement - fat pad and marrow both positive. First Dara-CyBorD treatment was Monday 3/15; tolerated it, a little wired the night after the dexamethasone. Sugars run in the 200s the morning after dex. Breathing about the same; legs still swell by evening. Taking furosemide every morning.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40, ASA 81, acetaminophen PRN. New: dexamethasone 20 mg weekly, acyclovir 400 BID. Weekly daratumumab, bortezomib and cyclophosphamide at the infusion center. NKDA.

O: Vitals reviewed. Lungs clear. Heart regular. 1-2+ edema to mid-shin.

A/P:
1. Systemic AL amyloidosis on Dara-CyBorD - hematology leads; we will keep his list current and handle everything else.
2. T2DM - expect steroid-day spikes. Check fasting and pre-supper sugars daily; send me the log in a month. Call for readings over 300 or lightheadedness. Continue metformin for now.
3. HFrEF / edema - cardiology co-managing; daily weights.
4. CKD 3b - labs are being drawn weekly at the infusion center; I will follow those.
Spent extended time answering questions. RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Sugar log
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, here is the month of sugars you asked for. Day after the dexamethasone (Tuesdays) they run 210 to 265 in the morning and about the same before supper. By Thursday they are back to 140s and the rest of the week 130 to 155. Highest was 271 once. No dizzy spells. Treatments are going ok, tired the day after. Herb Clark

documents.title: RE: Sugar log
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the careful log. That pattern is exactly what the weekly dexamethasone does and it settles within two days. As long as you stay under 300 and feel well, we will leave the metformin as it is - the dexamethasone part of your treatment is only for the first six months. Keep checking and let me know if anything changes. See you in June.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Cycle 4 of Dara-CyBorD. Hematology says light chains are falling. Tired, but walking again. Edema a bit less.
New issue: for a few months (thinks since around February) he has trouble getting a swallow started, coughs and sputters with drinks, sometimes chokes on food. Once or twice liquid came out his nose. No weight loss. No heartburn, no food sticking low in the chest. No fevers or pneumonia.
Sugars: steroid days 200s-260s, other days 140s.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 BID, furosemide 40, ASA 81, acetaminophen PRN, dexamethasone 20 mg weekly, acyclovir 400 BID; daratumumab/bortezomib/cyclophosphamide at infusion center. NKDA.

O: Vitals reviewed. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Edema 1+ ankles. Watched him drink water: brief cough after the second sip.

Labs: A1c 8.6 today.

A/P:
1. Swallowing difficulty with coughing on liquids and nasal regurgitation - sounds oropharyngeal rather than esophageal. GI referral; they can arrange a modified barium swallow. Meanwhile small sips, sit upright, slow down.
2. T2DM - A1c 8.6, driven by weekly dexamethasone, which stops after cycle 6 in August. Not adding a second agent now; recheck in fall off steroids.
3. AL amyloidosis - on treatment, hematology following.
4. HFrEF - stable to slightly better.
RTC after GI.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 08/02/2021
Referred by: primary care

History: Mr. Clark is a 69-year-old man with systemic AL amyloidosis (on therapy with hematology), lumbar spinal stenosis, HFrEF, CKD 3b, hypertension, type 2 diabetes - poorly controlled this year on steroid-containing chemotherapy, A1c 8.6 in June - and an ischemic stroke in 2017 with mild residual left-sided weakness. For about six months he has had trouble starting a swallow. He coughs and chokes often while eating, liquids more than solids, and occasionally has nasal regurgitation. No odynophagia, no retrosternal food impaction, no weight loss.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, furosemide 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, dexamethasone 20 mg weekly, acyclovir 400 mg BID, acetaminophen PRN; infusional daratumumab, bortezomib and cyclophosphamide.
Allergies: none known.
Family history: father MI at 62, hypertension; mother type 2 diabetes, stroke at 70; no amyloidosis or autoimmune disease.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, retired accountant.

Examination: Speech is slightly slurred. Gag reflex reduced. Oral cavity otherwise unremarkable. Abdomen benign.

Videofluoroscopic modified barium swallow (performed today with speech pathology): the swallow is slow to trigger; contrast pools in the valleculae; there is penetration into the laryngeal vestibule, without aspiration below the cords, across the consistencies tested.

Impression: Oropharyngeal dysphagia.

Recommendations:
1. Speech-language pathology for swallow therapy and strategies (referral placed).
2. Upright for all intake, small bites and sips.
3. No esophageal evaluation needed at this time given the oropharyngeal pattern.
4. Follow up as needed.

Gastroenterology

Date of service: 08/10/2021

Mr. Clark has completed six cycles of daratumumab, cyclophosphamide, bortezomib and dexamethasone. Fatigue improving. Swallowing being evaluated by GI.

Free lambda 24 mg/L, kappa 12 mg/L today (from 186 / 11 at diagnosis). This is a very good partial hematologic response.

2. Continue daratumumab 1800 mg subcutaneous every 4 weeks to complete two years of therapy (through March 2023).
3. Continue acyclovir while on daratumumab.
4. Free light chains every 3 months.

SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY - SWALLOW EVALUATION
Date of service: 08/24/2021
Referral: gastroenterology / primary care. Dx: oropharyngeal dysphagia.
Allergies: none known.

Background: modified barium swallow 08/02/2021 with delayed swallow trigger, vallecular pooling and laryngeal penetration without aspiration.

Clinical swallow today: delayed trigger with thin liquid by cup; throat clear after consecutive sips. Chin-tuck posture reduced coughing with thin liquids. Solids managed with a second swallow to clear.

Plan: 4 sessions of swallow therapy (effortful swallow, tongue-base and Shaker exercises), chin tuck with thin liquids, single small sips, double swallow with solids, upright 30 minutes after meals. Home program.

documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 01/29/2022, arrival 16:40

CC: short of breath, can't lie flat, legs swollen; "is this a reaction to my new pill?"

HPI: 69M with systemic AL amyloidosis on daratumumab, HFrEF, CAD with LAD stent, CKD 3b, HTN, T2DM, prior stroke. For a week, steadily worse breathlessness, now sleeping propped up, legs more swollen. Yesterday his upper lip swelled for a few hours; it went down on its own overnight. Hydrochlorothiazide was added about 11 weeks ago.

Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, furosemide 40, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5, metformin 1000 BID, aspirin 81, acyclovir 400 BID, daratumumab monthly.
Allergies on arrival: none known.

Exam: T 37.0 C, BP 135/78, P 88, RR 20. Lips and tongue without swelling now; airway patent, no stridor. JVD present. S3 gallop. Crackles in both lung fields. 2+ pitting edema of the lower extremities.

Data: Na 129, K 3.1. Chest x-ray: pulmonary edema.

ED course: IV furosemide with good urine output; oral potassium replacement. Breathing improved. Placed in observation overnight; sodium and potassium improving on morning recheck; comfortable lying at 30 degrees by morning.

Impression:
1. Pulmonary edema / volume overload in chronic HFrEF with cardiac amyloidosis.
2. Hyponatremia and hypokalemia with a reported episode of lip angioedema - adverse reaction to hydrochlorothiazide.

Disposition: discharged 01/30/2022. Hydrochlorothiazide stopped and entered as an allergy (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities). Continue furosemide 40 mg every morning. Follow up with primary care within 3-5 days and cardiology within 2 weeks. Return for breathlessness at rest, chest pain, or any lip or tongue swelling.

documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 11/01/2022
Referred by: primary care

HPI: 70-year-old man with systemic AL amyloidosis (daratumumab maintenance, hematologic response), HFrEF, CKD 3b and prior dyspnea work-ups, who has had two months of trouble getting up from chairs and going up stairs, with growing fatigue and some breathlessness on exertion. No trauma. No muscle cramps, no rash, no joint swelling.

PMH also: hypertension and type 2 diabetes, both well controlled (A1c 7.0 in July); CAD with LAD stent; lumbar spinal stenosis; oropharyngeal dysphagia; stroke 2017 with mild left-sided weakness.
Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, furosemide 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, acyclovir 400 mg BID, acetaminophen PRN, daratumumab monthly.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities).
Family history: no autoimmune disease or amyloidosis; father MI at 62; mother diabetes and stroke at 70.
Social: no tobacco, alcohol or drugs.

Exam: Weakness of the deltoids, biceps and quadriceps, symmetric on the two sides. Distal strength preserved. Deep tendon reflexes intact. Sensation intact. No heliotrope rash, Gottron papules or other rash. No synovitis.

Labs: creatine kinase 3,200 U/L (reference 22-198). ESR 72 mm/hr.

Impression: Proximal symmetric myopathy with a markedly raised CK and ESR - inflammatory myopathy (polymyositis) is most likely. Amyloid myopathy is in the differential given his history and needs to be excluded on biopsy.

Plan:
1. EMG/nerve conduction study.
2. Muscle biopsy (vastus lateralis) with Congo red stain.
3. Will start treatment once the biopsy is back.

reports.text:
NERVE CONDUCTION STUDY AND NEEDLE EMG
Indication: proximal weakness, CK 3,200.
Nerve conductions: sensory and motor studies in the right arm and leg are normal in amplitude, latency and velocity.
Needle EMG: right deltoid, biceps, iliopsoas and vastus lateralis show fibrillation potentials and short-duration, low-amplitude, polyphasic motor units with early recruitment. Distal muscles normal.
reports.conclusion: Irritable proximal myopathy. Normal nerve conduction studies.

procedures.procedure: Nerve conduction study with needle EMG

documents.title: EMG Report Received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: EMG/NCS report (11/15/2022) received from the outside neurophysiology lab, ordered by rheumatology. Scanned and routed to PCP.

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: skeletal muscle, right vastus lateralis, open biopsy.
Microscopic: Endomysial inflammatory infiltrates of lymphocytes surround and invade non-necrotic muscle fibers; immunostains show these are predominantly CD8-positive T cells. No perifascicular atrophy. No vasculitis.
Congo red: negative; no amyloid deposits.
reports.conclusion: Inflammatory myopathy with endomysial CD8 T cells invading non-necrotic fibers, consistent with polymyositis. No amyloid.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 12/06/2022

EMG: irritable proximal myopathy, normal nerve conductions. Muscle biopsy: endomysial CD8 T-cell inflammation invading non-necrotic fibers; Congo red negative, so no amyloid myopathy.

Diagnosis: Polymyositis.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 60 mg daily, with a taper planned once CK falls and strength returns.
2. TPMT activity sent; azathioprine as a steroid-sparing agent once it results. Methotrexate avoided given his kidney function.
3. Prednisone will raise glucose - please follow his diabetes closely.
4. CK and strength check in 4-5 weeks.
Allergies: hydrochlorothiazide (angioedema, electrolyte abnormalities).

documents.title: Prednisone and Glucose
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called patient per PCP after rheumatology letter. Started prednisone 60 mg daily on 12/7. Reviewed: check sugar fasting and before supper daily, write them down, send readings in 2 weeks or call for anything over 300, excessive thirst, or confusion. Take prednisone with breakfast. He has plenty of strips. Verbalized understanding.
Addendum (PCP): agree. Continue metformin; will adjust if sugars run high.
